# Re-verify ring definitions by checking which positions exist at rows 26 and 35
seg = current_frame.segmentation

for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['pixels'] == 4 and n['color'] not in ['B', 'N', 'G', 'c', 'R']:
        b = n['boundary']
        min_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
        min_c = min(p[1] for p in b)
        blocks[(min_r, min_c)] = n['color']

# Check row 26 positions

print(f"Row 26 positions: {row26}")

# Check row 35 positions

    if r not in rows:
        rows[r] = []
    rows[r].append(c)

print("\nAll rows with blocks:")
for r in sorted(rows.keys()):
    print(f"  Row {r}: {sorted(rows[r])}")

# Now let me do a probe: click middle_red and see what changes
# Save current state
current_blocks = dict(blocks)

action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 25, 'col': 13}])

# Check new state
seg2 = current_frame.segmentation
new_blocks = {}
for n in seg2['nodes']:
    if n['pixels'] == 4 and n['color'] not in ['B', 'N', 'G', 'c', 'R']:
        b = n['boundary']
        min_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
        min_c = min(p[1] for p in b)
        new_blocks[(min_r, min_c)] = n['color']

# Find changed positions
changed = []
for pos in set(list(current_blocks.keys()) + list(new_blocks.keys())):
    old = current_blocks.get(pos, '?')
    new = new_blocks.get(pos, '?')
    if old != new:
        changed.append((pos, old, new))

print(f"\nAfter middle_red, changed positions ({len(changed)}):")
for pos, old, new in sorted(changed):
    print(f"  {pos}: {old} -> {new}")
</parameter>
</function>
